claims.text: Introducing dual structure-composition heterogeneities into eutectic high-entropy alloys will simultaneously increase strength and ductility.
The initial material is an as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Dual structure-composition heterogeneities will be introduced through controlled solidification followed by thermomechanical processing.
A controlled cooling rate followed by annealing at 800°C for 2 hours will promote formation of a heterogeneous microstructure.
The dual structure-composition heterogeneities consist of FCC and BCC phases with varying elemental distributions.
The heterogeneous microstructure creates obstacles to dislocation motion.
Dual structure-composition heterogeneities facilitate strain accommodation.
Dual structure-composition heterogeneities reduce crack initiation and propagation, thereby promoting ductility.
The intervention will increase yield strength by 20% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The intervention will increase elongation to failure by 30% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The baseline as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy has a homogeneous microstructure.
The intervention is expected to be effective for Al0.5CoCrFeNi eutectic high-entropy alloys processed under the specified conditions.
The magnitude of the strength and ductility changes depends on alloy composition and processing conditions.
The hypothesis will be falsified if yield strength and elongation do not exceed baseline values by at least 15% and 20%, respectively.

contradictions.description: The predicted improvements are 20% in yield strength and 30% in elongation, but the falsification thresholds are only 15% and 20%. Results between those values would miss the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis, leaving an internally ambiguous decision region.
